I work with Go, Python, TypeScript, Next.js, and databases. I'm interested in AI/ML, data science, cybersecurity, and space technology. summary: Helm is a spaceflight crew health monitoring and decision-support demo for long-duration missions. It helps a crew track daily health indicators against personal pre-flight baselines, review trends and alerts, follow routines, and access educational emergency guidance. A live space-weather snapshot combines NASA DONKI and NOAA SWPC data. Helm uses simulated crew records and is not a certified medical device.
details:
Helm explores how a clear, crew-focused interface could support routine health check-ins during a long-duration space mission. Crew members can record seven health indicators heart rate, blood pressure, sleep, mood, body temperature, blood glucose, and exercise and compare readings with simulated personal pre-flight baselines. The app presents trends, context-aware status guidance, mission routines, body-system and hazard information, and a guided emergency-protocol demonstration.

The project pairs a Go HTTP API with a Next.js web frontend. The backend generates clearly labeled demo data, persists mission state locally as JSON, and periodically retrieves public NASA DONKI and NOAA SWPC space weather feeds for a cached radiation-environment snapshot. This is a hackathon decision-support concept: its sample data, thresholds, and emergency content are illustrative, not clinically validated, and must not replace approved mission procedures or professional medical care.
